Humyn Labs raises $47 million in equity and debt for real-world robot data

The financing comprises $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt, supporting vision, sound, touch and motion data collection.

The Robot Report ↗18 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Equity and debt are separate components

The Robot Report covered Humyn Labs’ financing on November 18. The $47 million total comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. The entire amount should therefore not be described as equity investment.

Collection programs tailored to research needs

The company uses proprietary capture devices and field partners in more than 20 countries to record vision, sound, touch and motion. Its enrichment process produces labeled data with verified provenance for model developers. Programs span residential, commercial and industrial work, focusing on task execution across different robot embodiments.

Investment in deployment readiness

Plans cover readiness infrastructure in Brazil, Korea and India, capture hardware and enrichment technology, and presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul. The company reports more than $50 million in annualized revenue after six months of operations. That is a run-rate figure, not a completed year of recognized revenue or proof of customer robot performance.
